end.summary:
Practised checking exact answers by estimating first.
Kabir estimated 48 × 25 using 50 × 25, but said around 1,000.
Discussed that an estimate should be close to the exact answer, not equal.
Kabir applied rounding to estimate 1,48,700 + 2,52,900 as about 4 lakh.
Teach-back was not passed; the exact-versus-estimate mix-up remained uncorrected at the last seen point.
end.parentNote: Asha practised estimating before checking an exact answer. Kabir used 50 × 25 to estimate 48 × 25 and later correctly explained that an estimate gives a nearby value, not the exact same number. They initially rejected 8,870 because it differed from 9,000, and this mix-up was still present when last seen. At home, ask Kabir to decide whether exact answers are reasonably close to estimates in two simple addition examples.
